title: Ratios that depend only on the angle
objectives: Define sine, cosine and tangent as ratios of the sides of a right-angled triangle
Explain why each ratio depends only on the angle, not the size

screens.title: Ratios that depend only on the angle
screens.prose: Two ramps can differ in size and still be equally steep. We will find numbers that measure the steepness and ignore the size.
A ramp rises 3 m over 4 m across. A longer ramp is built at exactly the same angle, along the same line, and runs 12 m across.

state.caption: Small ramp: 4 across, 3 up. Long ramp: 12 across, same angle.

screens.question: How high does the long ramp rise, in metres?

hints.text: How many times further across does the long ramp go?
12 across is three times 4 across.
Same angle means the same shape, so the rise is also three times as big: $3 \times 3$.

feedback.correct: Three times as far across, three times as high: 9 m.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare 12 across with 4 across, and scale the rise the same way.

byKey.added: You added 8 to the rise because the run grew by 8. Same angle means the same shape: the rise is multiplied, not added to.
byKey.same: That is the small ramp's rise. The long ramp goes three times as far, at the same steepness.
byKey.across: You copied the run. The rise is 3 for every 4 across, so it is less than the run.

explain.text: The long ramp goes $12 \div 4 = 3$ times as far, so it rises $3 \times 3 = 9$ m. Up ÷ across is $\tfrac{3}{4} = \tfrac{9}{12} = 0.75$ for both. The angle fixes that ratio, whatever the size.

canvas.caption: Small ramp: 4 across, 3 up. Long ramp: 12 across, same angle.

screens.prose: Drag B along the ramp. The triangle grows and shrinks, but the angle at O stays the same. The caption divides the up side by the slant.
screens.question: What happens to up ÷ slant as the triangle grows?

options.why: You expected a bigger triangle to give a bigger ratio. Up and slant grow by the same factor, so their ratio stays put.

options.text: It shrinks as the triangle grows
options.why: Drag B right and watch the caption: both sides grow together, so the ratio does not fall.

hints.text: Drag B far right, then far left, and read the caption each time.
Watch the up side and the slant together.
At 4 across the sides are 3 and 5. At 8 across they are 6 and 10. Both ratios are 0.6.

feedback.correct: Up ÷ slant is 0.6 at every size.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Drag B to two very different places and compare the caption.

explain.text: At 4 across the sides are 3 and 5; at 8 across they are 6 and 10. Both give $\tfrac{3}{5} = \tfrac{6}{10} = 0.6$. The ratio belongs to the angle, not to the size.

screens.prose: Now the slider tilts the ramp. More up per 1 across means a steeper ramp and a bigger angle at O. You can still drag B.

derive.caption: Up per 1 across {{fixed(m, 2)}}. Up ÷ slant = {{fixed((B.y - 1)/sqrt(pow(B.x - 1, 2) + pow(B.y - 1, 2)), 3)}}

screens.question: Make the ramp steeper. What happens to up ÷ slant?

options.why: You kept the old angle in mind. The slider changes the angle, and the ratio follows it.
A steeper ramp has a longer up side compared with the slant. Slide right and read the caption.
The slant is always longer than the up side, so up ÷ slant never reaches 1.

hints.text: Slide from 0.75 up to 2.5 and watch the caption.
The up side catches up with the slant as the ramp steepens.
At 0.75 the ratio is 0.600. At 2.5 it is about 0.928. It never reaches 1.

feedback.correct: A bigger angle gives a bigger up ÷ slant, always under 1.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Slide the steepness up and read the caption.

explain.text: Each angle has its own value of up ÷ slant: 0.600 at 0.75 up per across, 0.928 at 2.5. The ratio depends on the angle and only on the angle. That is what lets us name it.

screens.prose: Name each side from the angle $\theta$ at O. The hypotenuse faces the right angle. The **opposite** side faces $\theta$. The **adjacent** side touches $\theta$ and is not the hypotenuse. Then $$\sin\theta = \frac{\text{opp}}{\text{hyp}}, \quad \cos\theta = \frac{\text{adj}}{\text{hyp}}, \quad \tan\theta = \frac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}$$
screens.question: Up ÷ slant was the sine. What is $\tan\theta$ here?

options.why: That is opposite over hypotenuse, $\tfrac{6}{10}$: the sine. Tangent divides by the adjacent side.
That is adjacent over hypotenuse, $\tfrac{8}{10}$: the cosine.
You divided adjacent by opposite. Tangent is opposite over adjacent, $\tfrac{6}{8}$.

hints.text: Tangent uses the two sides that are not the hypotenuse.
Opposite is 6 and adjacent is 8.
$\tan\theta = \tfrac{6}{8} = 0.75$.

feedback.correct: $\tan\theta = \tfrac{6}{8} = 0.75$, the same as the ramp's up per across.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Tangent is opposite over adjacent.

explain.text: $\tan\theta = \tfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}} = \tfrac{6}{8} = 0.75$. That is the ramp's up per 1 across from the start. Here $\sin\theta = 0.6$ and $\cos\theta = 0.8$, the same as the 3, 4, 5 ramp: same angle, same ratios.

screens.prose: Same triangle, but now use the angle $\varphi$ at B, the top corner. The hypotenuse has not moved. The other two sides swap roles.
screens.question: What is $\sin\varphi$?

options.why: You kept the labels from the angle at O. Seen from B, the side facing the angle is OA, which is 8.
That is $\tfrac{8}{6}$, opposite over adjacent: the tangent of $\varphi$.
That is $\tfrac{6}{8}$, the tangent of the angle at O. The sine of $\varphi$ is opposite over hypotenuse, seen from B.

hints.text: Which side faces the corner B?
From B, the opposite side is OA, along the bottom.
$\sin\varphi = \tfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{hyp}} = \tfrac{8}{10}$.

feedback.correct: From B the opposite side is OA, so $\sin\varphi = \tfrac{8}{10}$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Name the sides again from the corner B.

explain.text: From B, OA faces the angle and AB touches it. So $\sin\varphi = \tfrac{8}{10} = 0.8$, which equals $\cos\theta$. Opposite and adjacent depend on which angle you stand at.

screens.prose: Here the across side is fixed at 3 and the slider sets the steepness. The caption shows all three ratios for the angle at O.
screens.question: Steepen the ramp all the way. Which ratio can be bigger than 1?

options.why: Sine divides by the hypotenuse, the longest side. So it stays below 1 however steep the ramp.
Cosine also divides by the hypotenuse, and it shrinks as the ramp steepens.
Slide past 1 up per across: the up side overtakes the across side, and tan passes 1.

hints.text: Slide to 3 and read the caption.
Only one ratio leaves out the hypotenuse.
Tangent is opposite over adjacent. Once up beats across, it is above 1.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Slide to the steepest ramp and compare the three numbers.

explain.text: At 3 up per across, tan is 3.000 while sin is 0.949 and cos is 0.316. Sine and cosine divide by the hypotenuse, so they stay between 0 and 1. Tangent passes 1 once the angle passes $45^\circ$, where up equals across.

screens.prose: This triangle hangs from its long top side PR. The right angle is at Q, at the bottom. We want the angle at R.
screens.question: Which fraction is $\cos R$?

options.why: You took PR as the adjacent side, because it touches R and lies flat. PR faces the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse.
That is opposite over hypotenuse, the sine of R. Cosine uses the side next to R.
That is opposite over adjacent, the tangent of R. Cosine divides by the hypotenuse.

hints.text: Find the right angle first, then the side facing it.
The right angle is at Q, so PR is the hypotenuse. Two sides touch R: PR and QR.
QR touches R and is not the hypotenuse, so it is adjacent. $\cos R = \tfrac{QR}{PR}$.

feedback.correct: QR is adjacent and PR is the hypotenuse, so $\cos R = \tfrac{8}{10}$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the hypotenuse first, then the other side touching R.

byKey.hyp-adj: You used PR as the adjacent side because it touches R and lies flat. PR faces the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse, and it goes on the bottom.
byKey.tan: You divided by the adjacent side. That is the tangent; cosine divides by the hypotenuse.

explain.text: Both PR and QR touch R, but PR faces the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse. The adjacent side is the other one, QR. So $\cos R = \tfrac{8}{10} = 0.8$, and a cosine above 1, like $\tfrac{10}{8}$, is a sure sign of a mix-up.

screens.prose: Why does the size never matter? Take any right-angled triangle with angle $\theta$, and scale it by a factor $k$, as the long ramp did with $k = 3$. The angles do not change.

state.caption: Small ramp: 4 across, 3 up. Long ramp: 12 across, same angle.

screens.question: Put the lines of the argument in order.

lines.text: The big triangle has sides $k \cdot \text{opp}$, $k \cdot \text{adj}$ and $k \cdot \text{hyp}$: scaling multiplies every side by $k$
Its opposite over hypotenuse is $\dfrac{k \cdot \text{opp}}{k \cdot \text{hyp}}$: the same ratio, read in the big triangle
$= \dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{hyp}}$: the factor $k$ cancels, top and bottom
So $\sin\theta$ is the same at every size: it depends on $\theta$ alone

hints.text: Start with what scaling does to the sides.
The long ramp had every side three times the small one's.
Scale the sides, form the ratio, cancel $k$, conclude.

feedback.correct: Every side carries the same $k$, so it cancels in any ratio.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Begin with the scaled sides, and end with the conclusion.

byKey.cancel: You can only cancel $k$ once the ratio with $k$ in it is written.
byKey.concl: The conclusion comes after the cancelling.

explain.text: The scaled sides all carry the same $k$, so $\tfrac{k \cdot \text{opp}}{k \cdot \text{hyp}} = \tfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{hyp}}$. The same cancelling works for cosine and tangent. That is why one number per angle is enough.

screens.prose: A share trades in a rising channel: a support line below the price and a parallel resistance line above it. Support climbs £1.00 every 4 days. Parallel lines make the same angle with the time axis.
screens.question: Over a 10-day stretch, how far does the resistance line rise?

widget.label: Rise of the resistance line over 10 days
widget.accept: £2.50, from a gradient of 0.25 per day.

hints.text: What is the support line's rise per day?
Support rises £1.00 over 4 days: up ÷ across is 0.25.
Same angle, same ratio: the resistance line also rises £0.25 a day. Multiply by 10.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the rise per day on the support line, then use it on the resistance line.

byKey.unscaled: £1.00 was the rise over 4 days. The stretch here is 10 days.
byKey.added: You added 6 because the days grew by 6. Same angle means the rise is scaled, not added to.
byKey.flipped: You divided across by up. The gradient is up ÷ across: £1.00 per 4 days.
byKey.gap: £3.00 is the gap between the two lines. The question asks how far one line rises.

explain.text: Support rises $\tfrac{1.00}{4} = 0.25$ per day, and resistance is parallel, so it rises 0.25 a day too: $0.25 \times 10 =$ £2.50. On a chart where a day and £1 take the same length, 0.25 is the tangent of the line's angle. Parallel lines share that gradient, so a longer window only scales the rise.

ideas: Name the sides from the angle: the hypotenuse faces the right angle, the opposite side faces the angle, the adjacent side touches it.
Scaling a triangle multiplies every side by the same factor, so each ratio depends only on the angle.
Sine and cosine stay below 1, because they divide by the longest side. Tangent can be any size.

formula.name: The three ratios
formula.note: Read the sides from the angle you use. Move to the other angle and opposite and adjacent swap. UK classes remember the three ratios as SOH CAH TOA.

summary.trap: The hypotenuse touches the angle too. Find it first: the adjacent side is the other side that touches the angle.

quiz.prose: For an angle $\theta$ in a right-angled triangle, the opposite side is 5, the adjacent side is 12 and the hypotenuse is 13.
quiz.question: What is $\cos\theta$?

options.why: That is opposite over hypotenuse, the sine.
That is opposite over adjacent, the tangent.
You put the hypotenuse on top. A cosine is never above 1.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse.

explain.text: Cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse, so $\cos\theta = \tfrac{12}{13} \approx 0.923$.

quiz.prose: A right-angled triangle with hypotenuse 5 has $\sin\theta = 0.6$. It is enlarged so that the hypotenuse becomes 20, keeping its angles.
quiz.question: What is $\sin\theta$ in the enlarged triangle?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask whether the angle changed.

byKey.scaled: You multiplied the ratio by 4. The sides grow by 4, but top and bottom grow together.
byKey.side: 12 is the new opposite side. The sine is $\tfrac{12}{20}$.
byKey.quarter: You divided by 4. The ratio does not shrink either.

explain.text: Enlarging multiplies the opposite side and the hypotenuse by 4: $\tfrac{12}{20} = 0.6$. The angle is unchanged, so the sine is unchanged.

quiz.prose: A right-angled triangle has sides 8, 15 and 17. The side of length 8 faces the angle $\theta$.
quiz.question: What is $\tan\theta$?

options.why: You divided adjacent by opposite. Tangent is opposite over adjacent.
That divides by the hypotenuse: the sine. Tangent leaves the hypotenuse out.
That is adjacent over hypotenuse, the cosine.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The hypotenuse is 17, the longest; the adjacent side is the other one.

explain.text: 17 is the hypotenuse, 8 is opposite and 15 is adjacent. So $\tan\theta = \tfrac{8}{15} \approx 0.533$.

quiz.prose: A classmate claims a very steep angle has $\sin\theta = 1.2$.
quiz.question: Is that possible in a right-angled triangle?

options.text: No: the opposite side would be longer than the hypotenuse
Yes: close to $90^\circ$ the opposite side is longest
options.why: You are thinking of tangent, which does pass 1. Sine divides by the longest side.

options.text: Yes: a big enough triangle stretches the ratio past 1
options.why: Size never changes a ratio: top and bottom scale together.

feedback.correct: The hypotenuse is the longest side, so sine is below 1.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the opposite side with the hypotenuse.

explain.text: $\sin\theta = 1.2$ needs the opposite side to be 1.2 times the hypotenuse. But the hypotenuse is the longest side. So sine and cosine always lie between 0 and 1 in a right-angled triangle.
